title: Death Meaning: Bring What Has Ended to a Close

sections.title: The rider carries no scythe, and the flag bears a flower
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A skeleton in black armour rides a white horse toward the right of the picture. It carries a black flag bearing a white five-petalled flower, with no visible sword, scythe or other blade. The white horse fills the centre, lifting a foreleg and drawing the eye toward the figures ahead.

At lower left, a person lies on the ground near a fallen gold crown. On the right, a figure in a tall headdress and gold ceremonial robes faces the rider with hands together. Lower down are a kneeling child and a young person turning their face aside. A small boat is visible on the water in the background, and a radiant sun appears between two distant towers. The black-and-white banner, people of different stations and light in the distance place ending and continuation in the same picture. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_13_Death.jpg)

sections.title: Renewal still carries the weight of an ending
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Waite calls the flower on the banner the Mystic Rose and connects it with life. He places the distant sun in a religious context of immortality. His discussion includes change, passage and the transformation of consciousness without removing the weight of death imagery. Saying “nothing upsetting is really involved” makes the picture thinner than his account. [Waite, Part II, XIII](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar13.htm)

Our reading is symbolic and grounded in everyday life. Drawing this card cannot predict anyone’s death, illness or lifespan. It is more useful for considering a stage that has already ended, or an ending for which there is real-world evidence.

sections.title: Upright: Closing things is work too
sections.bodyMarkdown:
An upright reading may suggest acknowledging that an old form can no longer continue: a project ends, an identity changes, or a habit stops being useful. Practical farewells often follow, such as returning possessions, completing a handover, organising records or allowing time to adjust.

The next stage need not feel exciting immediately. You can know change is necessary and still miss what came before. Acknowledging both feelings is more honest than demanding instant positivity. The card cannot prove that a relationship must end; major decisions still depend on real circumstances.

sections.title: Reversed: Loosen one thing at the old threshold
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The reversed card can help you notice unfinished farewells: declaring something over while continually reopening it, or postponing every practical task to avoid sadness. Waite’s reversed list includes inertia and petrifaction, a historical link with being stuck. We extend that into reflection on delayed closure and fear of change. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 13](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

Adjustment may also simply take time. Do not turn “I have not let go yet” into another accusation against yourself. Separate responsibilities that need attention from feelings you can work through at your own pace.

sections.title: Turn an ending into actions you can complete
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A project closes after two years. Record the completed work, materials to hand over and what will no longer continue. A brief review lets people carry the learning forward and stops old tasks quietly occupying their time.

Before leaving a long-loved home, take photographs, then decide what to keep and what to give away. The memories can remain without every object having to prove that the life you lived there mattered.

If a habit is clearly disrupting daily life, such as repeatedly checking messages at night, start by silencing notifications for one period or moving your phone away from the bed. You do not have to begin with a sweeping promise to change forever.

sections.title: Practice: Make a gentle closing list
sections.bodyMarkdown: Choose something that has genuinely ended. List three actions still needed, then add “What I want to keep from this is…” Complete the smallest task first. If the loss is still heavy, support from someone you trust can matter more than rushing to find a hidden benefit.

articleMarkdown:
# Death Meaning: Bring What Has Ended to a Close

Card: Death  
Number: XIII · RWS Major Arcana  
Keywords: Endings, Transformation, Farewell

**Upright quick take:** This stage is ready to close. Finish the old business and make room for what comes next.  
**Reversed quick take:** You know something needs to change, but letting go is hard. Start with one old tie you can loosen.

Some changes need more than another small repair. Death puts an ending in view, making room both to acknowledge loss and to deal with the next stage.

## The rider carries no scythe, and the flag bears a flower

A skeleton in black armour rides a white horse toward the right of the picture. It carries a black flag bearing a white five-petalled flower, with no visible sword, scythe or other blade. The white horse fills the centre, lifting a foreleg and drawing the eye toward the figures ahead.

At lower left, a person lies on the ground near a fallen gold crown. On the right, a figure in a tall headdress and gold ceremonial robes faces the rider with hands together. Lower down are a kneeling child and a young person turning their face aside. A small boat is visible on the water in the background, and a radiant sun appears between two distant towers. The black-and-white banner, people of different stations and light in the distance place ending and continuation in the same picture. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_13_Death.jpg)

## Renewal still carries the weight of an ending

Waite calls the flower on the banner the Mystic Rose and connects it with life. He places the distant sun in a religious context of immortality. His discussion includes change, passage and the transformation of consciousness without removing the weight of death imagery. Saying “nothing upsetting is really involved” makes the picture thinner than his account. [Waite, Part II, XIII](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar13.htm)

Our reading is symbolic and grounded in everyday life. Drawing this card cannot predict anyone’s death, illness or lifespan. It is more useful for considering a stage that has already ended, or an ending for which there is real-world evidence.

## Upright: Closing things is work too

An upright reading may suggest acknowledging that an old form can no longer continue: a project ends, an identity changes, or a habit stops being useful. Practical farewells often follow, such as returning possessions, completing a handover, organising records or allowing time to adjust.

The next stage need not feel exciting immediately. You can know change is necessary and still miss what came before. Acknowledging both feelings is more honest than demanding instant positivity. The card cannot prove that a relationship must end; major decisions still depend on real circumstances.

## Reversed: Loosen one thing at the old threshold

The reversed card can help you notice unfinished farewells: declaring something over while continually reopening it, or postponing every practical task to avoid sadness. Waite’s reversed list includes inertia and petrifaction, a historical link with being stuck. We extend that into reflection on delayed closure and fear of change. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 13](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

Adjustment may also simply take time. Do not turn “I have not let go yet” into another accusation against yourself. Separate responsibilities that need attention from feelings you can work through at your own pace.

## Turn an ending into actions you can complete

A project closes after two years. Record the completed work, materials to hand over and what will no longer continue. A brief review lets people carry the learning forward and stops old tasks quietly occupying their time.

Before leaving a long-loved home, take photographs, then decide what to keep and what to give away. The memories can remain without every object having to prove that the life you lived there mattered.

If a habit is clearly disrupting daily life, such as repeatedly checking messages at night, start by silencing notifications for one period or moving your phone away from the bed. You do not have to begin with a sweeping promise to change forever.

## Practice: Make a gentle closing list

Choose something that has genuinely ended. List three actions still needed, then add “What I want to keep from this is…” Complete the smallest task first. If the loss is still heavy, support from someone you trust can matter more than rushing to find a hidden benefit.

## A common misreading

Death is neither a death notice nor a promise that everything will immediately improve. It invites attention to the reality of endings and the possibility of closure. When and how to end something depend on facts, choices and practical support.

## Read next

The Hanged Man: compare a pause with being unable to continue as before; Temperance: explore how to rebalance life after a change.

- [A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part II, §2, XIII Death](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar13.htm)

sourceRecord.hook: 有些改变不能只靠修修补补。死神把「结束」摆到眼前，让你承认失去，也腾出处理下一阶段的空间。

sections.title: 骑士没有镰刀，旗上却有一朵花
paragraphs: 身披黑色盔甲的骷髅骑在白马上，朝画面右侧前进。它举着黑旗，旗上是一朵白色五瓣花；手边没有可见的刀剑或镰刀。白马占据画面中央，前腿抬起，把视线带向前方的人群。

左下方有人倒在地上，附近散落着金色王冠。右侧，一位戴高冠、穿金色礼服的人合拢双手面对骑士；更低处有跪坐的小孩与侧过脸的年轻人。背景水面上还有一只小船，远处两座塔之间露出带光芒的太阳。黑白旗面、不同身份的人物与远景的光同处一幅图中，使「终结」与「仍在继续」同时可见。[查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_13_Death.jpg)

sections.title: 更新的象征，保留了终结的重量
paragraphs: Waite 把黑旗上的花解释为神秘玫瑰，与生命相连，又把远方的太阳放进不朽的宗教语境。他讨论改变、经过与意识转化，同时没有删去死亡意象自身的分量。因而，把这张牌说成「其实完全没有难过的事」，也会把画面读薄。[Waite 第二部 XIII](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar13.htm)
这里采用象征性的生活阅读。抽到此牌不能预测任何人的死亡、疾病或寿命；它更适合帮助你面对已经发生、或确有现实迹象的阶段结束。

sections.title: 正位 收尾也是一项工作
paragraphs: 正位可读作承认某种旧形式已无法继续：一项计划结束、一段身份改变、一种习惯失去作用。接下来往往需要处理具体的告别工作，例如归还物品、完成交接、整理档案，或给自己一段适应时间。
新阶段并不一定立刻令人振奋。你可以同时知道改变有必要，又舍不得原来的人事物。承认这份复杂，比强迫自己马上积极更诚实。牌不会替你证明一段关系必须结束；重大决定仍要看现实事实。

sections.title: 逆位 卡在旧门口时，先松一小处
paragraphs: 逆位常可用于观察迟迟无法完成的告别：嘴上说结束，行动却不断重开；或者为了避开难过，把所有整理一直往后推。Waite 的逆位词表包含惰性与僵化，为「停住」提供历史线索；本篇把它延伸成对拖延收尾、害怕变化的反思。[Waite 第三部 §3，第13条](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)
也可能只是适应需要时间。不要把「还没放下」变成新的责备，先辨认哪些责任必须处理，哪些情绪可以慢慢经历。

sections.title: 结束怎样变成可完成的动作
paragraphs: 一个做了两年的项目被正式关闭。先写清已完成成果、待移交材料与不再继续的范围；举行简短复盘，能让大家带走经验，避免旧任务仍偷偷占用时间。
搬离住了很久的房间，可先拍照留念，再决定什么带走、什么送出。纪念能够留下，不必靠保存每一件东西来证明那段生活重要。
某个习惯已明显影响你的日常，例如夜里不断刷消息。可以先关闭一个时段的通知、把手机移出床边，而不是给自己许下「从此彻底改变」的大承诺。

sections.title: 练习 写一份温和的收尾单
paragraphs: 列出一件确已结束的事，写下还要完成的三个动作，再补一句「我想留下的是什么」。选最小的一项处理。若现实中的失落仍很沉重，让可信赖的人陪伴，比急着找出隐藏的好处更有帮助。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 死神既不是死亡通知，也不是「一切都会马上更好」的保证。它提醒的是结束的现实与收尾的可能；何时结束、怎样结束，要由事实、选择和实际支持来决定。
